sentences.text: Suchomimus possessed an elongated, low, and narrow skull that strongly resembled that of modern crocodilians.
The animal had a relatively short neck and powerfully built forelimbs featuring a large curved claw on each thumb.
A low dorsal sail ran along the midline of its back, constructed from long neural spines.
The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, is catalogued as MNN GDF500 and consists of a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
Historical estimates placed the creature at 9.5 to 11 meters in length and 2.5 to 3.8 metric tons in weight.
The only known species, S. tenerensis, was described in 1998 by Paul Sereno and colleagues based on fossils found in the Elrhaz Formation.
The specific name 'tenerensis' refers to the Ténéré Desert where the fossils were discovered.
Suchomimus tenerensis was formally named and described in a study published in Science Magazine on November 13, 1998.
All known fossil specimens are currently housed in the collections of the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.
Isotopic geochemical evidence supports a semi-aquatic foraging habit for Suchomimus.
Researchers generally view Suchomimus as a large creature that usually fed on fish and walked through the Sahara over 100 million years ago when it was a swampy paradise.
Suchomimus is classified within the family Spinosauridae.
The genus belongs to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
In its original description, Suchomimus was placed within Spinosauridae and assigned to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
In 2021, American paleontologist Chris T. Barker and colleagues established the tribe Ceratosuchopsini within Baryonychinae, which includes Ceratosuchops, Riparovenator, and Suchomimus.
Suchomimus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically the Aptian to Albian stages.
Suchomimus lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago, in the Aptian stage.
Suchomimus lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
Suchomimus lived in what is now Africa.
Cristatusaurus lapparenti was named by Philippe Taquet and Dale A. Russell more than two months before Suchomimus tenerensis was formally described.

A 2017 review by Carlos Roberto A. Candeiro and colleagues stated the debate over Suchomimus and Baryonyx is more semantic than scientific, noting they are generally agreed to be distinct related genera.
In 2010, British paleontologist Roger Benson considered the superfamily Spinosauroidea a junior synonym of Megalosauroidea.
Milner suggested in 2003 that spinosaurids originated in Laurasia during the Jurassic and dispersed into Gondwana via the Iberian land bridge.
The direction of dispersal between Europe and Africa for spinosaurids is still unknown.
